parts.title: Orientation
parts.summary: What Sanskrit is, which Sanskrit this guide teaches, the organising idea of roots, stems, endings and joins, and how the guide prints Sanskrit.

parts.title: Sounds and script
parts.summary: The sound grid behind the alphabet, vowels and consonants with their IPA values, Devanagari built up in stages (inherent a, vowel signs, virāma, conjuncts, the special signs, numerals), and IAST and Unicode as used in the guide.

parts.title: The simplest sentences
parts.summary: Subject and verb, the object, persons and numbers including the dual, gender and agreement, the first sandhi rules, being, negation, coordination and questions, the vocative and iti.

parts.title: Nouns and their machinery
parts.summary: The remaining five cases, the a- and ā-stems complete, vowel sandhi, the pronouns, guṇa and vṛddhi, and the other stem types from i- and u-stems to consonant stems with three grades, and the irregular nouns.

parts.title: Verbs: the core system
parts.summary: Roots and present classes, the middle voice, the imperfect, prefixes, imperative and optative, consonant sandhi, the athematic classes, the past participle and passive, converb and infinitive, future, perfect, aorist and the present participles.

parts.title: Modifying and linking
parts.summary: Adjectives, pronominal adjectives, adverbs and prepositional words, linking particles, numbers, comparison, internal sandhi, and five lessons on compounds.

parts.title: Complex sentences
parts.summary: Question words and indefinites, relative and correlative clauses, reported speech with iti, purpose and cause, conditions, the gerundive, participial clauses and the locative absolute.

parts.title: Advanced and special topics
parts.summary: Causative, desiderative, intensive and denominative verbs, word formation, rare verb forms, metre, epic Sanskrit, learned styles, Vedic Sanskrit, and Pāṇini and the tradition.

parts.title: Reading real texts
parts.summary: Seven graded passages from the Hitopadeśa, the Nala episode of the Mahābhārata, the Rāmāyaṇa, the Bhagavad Gītā and Kālidāsa, ending with a capstone on the opening of the Gītā and its most famous verse.

parts.title: Reference
parts.summary: Paradigm tables for nouns, pronouns and verbs, sandhi tables, glossary of terms and abbreviations, annotated bibliography.

lessons.title: What Sanskrit is
lessons.point: Place Sanskrit in time, space and family, and know which Sanskrit this guide teaches and why

lessons.title: The organising idea: roots, stems, endings and joins
lessons.point: See how a root becomes a stem and a stem takes an ending, why vowels grow (guṇa, vṛddhi), and why words fuse at their edges (sandhi)

lessons.title: How to use this guide
lessons.point: Read the example blocks, the transliteration toggle, the unjoined and joined forms, and the source labels

lessons.title: The sound system: the grid behind the alphabet
lessons.point: See how the Indian phoneticians ordered the sounds by place and manner, and why that order runs the whole grammar

lessons.title: The vowels: length, the vocalic ṛ and the diphthongs
lessons.point: Pronounce the vowels, hold short and long apart, say ṛ as a vowel, and tell heavy from light syllables

lessons.title: The stops: five places, four kinds
lessons.point: Pronounce the 25 stops and nasals, including aspirates and retroflexes

lessons.title: Semivowels, sibilants, h, anusvāra and visarga
lessons.point: Pronounce y r l v, the three s-sounds, h, and the two sounds that exist only at the edges of syllables

lessons.title: Devanagari I: consonant letters and the inherent a
lessons.point: Read and write the consonant letters, each of which carries an a unless told otherwise

lessons.title: Devanagari II: vowel letters and vowel signs
lessons.point: Write any vowel at the start of a word as a letter and after a consonant as a sign

lessons.title: Devanagari III: virāma and conjunct consonants
lessons.point: Kill the inherent a with virāma and read the common stacked and joined consonant clusters

lessons.title: Devanagari IV: the special signs, punctuation and numerals
lessons.point: Read anusvāra, visarga, candrabindu, avagraha, daṇḍa, oṃ and the Devanagari digits

lessons.title: Transliteration, Unicode and how joined words are printed
lessons.point: Transliterate Devanagari into IAST and back, type both correctly, and read a line in which words run together

lessons.title: A first sentence: who does it and what happens
lessons.point: Say 'the god goes' with a nominative a-stem and a third-person present verb

lessons.title: The object: the accusative
lessons.point: Add a direct object or a goal of motion, and see why word order is free

lessons.title: I, you, they: persons and the plural
lessons.point: Conjugate a present verb in all persons, singular and plural, and use aham, tvam, vayam, yūyam

lessons.title: Exactly two: the dual
lessons.point: Use the dual of verbs and of a-stem nouns for any pair

lessons.title: Three genders and adjectives that agree
lessons.point: Tell masculine, neuter and feminine a- and ā-stems apart and make an adjective agree

lessons.title: Joining words I: final -ḥ and -m
lessons.point: Join words as texts do at the commonest points: -aḥ before a consonant or vowel, and final -m

lessons.title: Being: as, and the sentence without a verb
lessons.point: Say that something is something, with or without asti

lessons.title: Not, and, or, and yes/no questions
lessons.point: Negate with na, join with ca and vā, stress with eva and api, and ask with kim and api

lessons.title: Calling and quoting: the vocative and iti
lessons.point: Address someone, and quote what was said or thought with iti

lessons.title: Review: part 2 as a whole
lessons.point: Translate a passage and build and correct sentences using everything taught so far

lessons.title: The instrumental: with and by
lessons.point: Say with whom and by what means, and meet the n-to-ṇ rule

lessons.title: The dative: to and for
lessons.point: Say to whom something is given and what it is for

lessons.title: The ablative: from and because
lessons.point: Say where something comes from and why

lessons.title: The genitive: of and whose
lessons.point: Say whose and of what, and use the genitive with verbs and adjectives

lessons.title: The locative: in, on, at and when
lessons.point: Say where and when, and among whom

lessons.title: The a- and ā-stems complete
lessons.point: Decline any masculine or neuter a-stem and feminine ā-stem in all eight cases and three numbers

lessons.title: Joining words II: vowel meets vowel
lessons.point: Join and split words where a final vowel meets an initial vowel

lessons.title: I, you, we: the personal pronouns in full
lessons.point: Use aham and tvam in all cases and numbers, including the short enclitic forms

lessons.title: He, she, that: sa, sā, tad and eṣa
lessons.point: Use the demonstrative as 'that' and as 'he, she, it', and know its pronominal endings

lessons.title: Review: putting it together so far
lessons.point: Translate, build and correct sentences using everything taught up to here

lessons.title: Vowel grades: guṇa and vṛddhi
lessons.point: Know the three grades of each vowel and predict them; see why they explain irregularity everywhere

lessons.title: Stems in -i and -u
lessons.point: Decline agni, mati, guru and dhenu, and see guṇa at work in their endings

lessons.title: Feminines in -ī and -ū
lessons.point: Decline nadī, devī and vadhū, and form feminines of nouns and adjectives

lessons.title: Stems in -ṛ: strong and weak forms
lessons.point: Decline pitṛ, mātṛ and dātṛ, and understand strong and weak cases

lessons.title: Consonant stems with one form
lessons.point: Decline vāc, marut and manas, and see why the stem's last consonant changes before -bh- and -su

lessons.title: Stems in -an and -man: three grades
lessons.point: Decline rājan, ātman, nāman and karman with their strong, middle and weakest stems

lessons.title: Stems in -vat, -mat and -in
lessons.point: Decline bhagavat and balin, and recognise 'having X' adjectives

lessons.title: This here, that yonder: ayam, idam and asau
lessons.point: Use the near and far demonstratives with their mixed stems

lessons.title: The irregular nouns
lessons.point: Recognise the common irregular nouns: pums, strī, go, dyo, ap, path, ahan, sakhi, pati

lessons.title: Review: part 3 as a whole
lessons.point: Translate a passage and build and correct sentences using everything taught so far

lessons.title: Roots and the four thematic classes
lessons.point: Find the present stem of any class 1, 4, 6 or 10 verb from its root

lessons.title: The middle voice
lessons.point: Conjugate and understand middle verbs, and verbs used in both voices

lessons.title: The imperfect: telling what happened
lessons.point: Narrate the past with the augment and the secondary endings

lessons.title: Verbal prefixes
lessons.point: Recognise the twenty prefixes, see how they change a root's meaning, and place the augment after them

lessons.title: Commands: the imperative
lessons.point: Give orders, make requests and say 'let him', 'let us'

lessons.title: Wishes, rules and possibilities: the optative
lessons.point: Say 'may he', 'one should' and 'he would', and read rules and advice

lessons.title: Joining words III: final consonants
lessons.point: Join any word ending in a consonant to the next word, and undo the join

lessons.title: Athematic verbs I: the root class
lessons.point: Conjugate as, i, ad, han, brū and vid, with their strong and weak stems

lessons.title: Athematic verbs II: the reduplicating class
lessons.point: Conjugate dā, dhā, hu and bhī, and see reduplication as a present stem

lessons.title: Review: putting it together so far
lessons.point: Translate, build and correct sentences using everything taught up to here

lessons.title: Athematic verbs III: the nu- and u-classes, and kṛ
lessons.point: Conjugate śak, āp, tan and the irregular kṛ 'do, make'

lessons.title: Athematic verbs IV: the nā-class and the nasal-infix class
lessons.point: Conjugate krī, jñā and grah, and yuj, rudh and bhid

lessons.title: The past participle in -ta and -na
lessons.point: Form and use the past participle, the commonest past tense of later prose, and the active participle in -tavat

lessons.title: The passive
lessons.point: Form the present passive, put the agent in the instrumental, and read impersonal passives

lessons.title: One action, then another: the converb in -tvā and -ya
lessons.point: Chain actions with the converb, the backbone of Sanskrit narrative

lessons.title: The infinitive in -tum
lessons.point: Say 'to do' after verbs of wanting, being able and deserving, and for purpose

lessons.title: The future
lessons.point: Form and use the s-future and the periphrastic future

lessons.title: The perfect
lessons.point: Form the reduplicated perfect, read it as the narrative past of the epics, and know uvāca, jagāma, babhūva, āha and veda

lessons.title: The aorist, and mā with the injunctive
lessons.point: Recognise the main aorist types, and forbid with mā and an unaugmented aorist

lessons.title: Present participles
lessons.point: Form and decline the active participle in -at and the middle participle in -māna and -āna

lessons.title: Review: part 4 as a whole
lessons.point: Translate a passage and build and correct sentences using everything taught so far

lessons.title: Adjectives: agreement, order and use as nouns
lessons.point: Use adjectives of every stem type attributively, predicatively and as nouns

lessons.title: All, other, one: the pronominal adjectives
lessons.point: Decline sarva, anya, para, eka and their kind with pronominal endings

lessons.title: Adverbs, and the words that do the work of prepositions
lessons.point: Form adverbs from cases and suffixes, and use saha, vinā, prati, upari and others with the right case

lessons.title: Linking particles: tu, hi, atha, tataḥ, evam
lessons.point: Mark contrast, reason, sequence and summary between sentences

lessons.title: Numbers
lessons.point: Count, decline eka, dvi, tri and catur, and use ordinals and the higher numbers

lessons.title: Comparison: -tara, -tama, -īyas, -iṣṭha
lessons.point: Say bigger and biggest, and compare with the ablative

lessons.title: Inside the word: internal sandhi
lessons.point: Predict the sound changes inside words (ṣ after i, u, ṛ, k, r; ṇ after ṛ, r, ṣ; consonant clashes) that make paradigms look irregular

lessons.title: Compounds I: what a compound is, and dependent compounds
lessons.point: Read and build tatpuruṣa compounds, where one member depends on the other in some case

lessons.title: Compounds II: descriptive and number compounds
lessons.point: Read karmadhāraya compounds (adjective + noun, 'X like Y') and dvigu compounds

lessons.title: Compounds III: copulative compounds
lessons.point: Read dvandva compounds ('X and Y') and choose their number and gender

lessons.title: Compounds IV: possessive compounds
lessons.point: Read bahuvrīhi compounds, which describe something else that has X

lessons.title: Compounds V: adverbial compounds and long compounds
lessons.point: Read avyayībhāva compounds and take apart a compound of many members step by step

lessons.title: Review: part 5 as a whole
lessons.point: Translate a passage and build and correct sentences using everything taught so far

lessons.title: Question words and indefinites
lessons.point: Ask who, what, where, when, how and why, and turn each into 'someone, somewhere' with cid, cana and api

lessons.title: Relative clauses: ya ... sa
lessons.point: Build the Sanskrit relative sentence, where a ya- clause is picked up by a sa- word

lessons.title: When, where, as, as long as: correlative pairs
lessons.point: Use yadā–tadā, yatra–tatra, yathā–tathā, yāvat–tāvat and their kin

lessons.title: Reported speech and thought with iti
lessons.point: Report words, thoughts, names and reasons with iti, and read iti-clauses inside long sentences

lessons.title: Purpose and cause
lessons.point: Say why and what for with the infinitive, dative, artham, hi, yataḥ and the ablative

lessons.title: Conditions: yadi, the optative and the conditional
lessons.point: Build real, possible and unreal conditions

lessons.title: Must and should: the gerundive
lessons.point: Form and use the future passive participle in -tavya, -anīya and -ya

lessons.title: Participles as clauses, and the locative absolute
lessons.point: Read participles that stand for whole clauses, and the locative and genitive absolute

lessons.title: Review: part 6 as a whole
lessons.point: Translate a passage and build and correct sentences using everything taught so far

lessons.title: The causative
lessons.point: Form and use the causative in -aya-, the periphrastic perfect, and see why class 10 looks the same

lessons.title: The desiderative
lessons.point: Form and use the desiderative 'want to do', and its nouns and adjectives

lessons.title: The intensive and the denominative
lessons.point: Recognise intensive verbs and make verbs from nouns

lessons.title: Building nouns from roots: primary suffixes
lessons.point: Recognise the main kṛt suffixes (-a, -ana, -ti, -tṛ, -man, -as, -tra) and the vowel grade each takes

lessons.title: Building words from words: vṛddhi and secondary suffixes
lessons.point: Recognise taddhita derivatives such as pāṇḍava, śaiva, -tva, -tā, -ka, -ya, -maya

lessons.title: Rare verb forms: the precative and others
lessons.point: Recognise the precative, the rarer aorists and other forms met mainly in verse

lessons.title: Metre: the śloka and other verse
lessons.point: Scan a śloka and a triṣṭubh line, and see how metre bends word order and form

lessons.title: Epic Sanskrit and ārṣa forms
lessons.point: Recognise what the epics do that Pāṇini's grammar does not allow, and why

lessons.title: Learned styles: śāstra prose and kāvya
lessons.point: Read the nominal style of the commentaries and the ornate style of court poetry

lessons.title: Vedic Sanskrit
lessons.point: Know what the older language has that Classical lacks: pitch accent, subjunctive, many infinitives, older forms

lessons.title: Pāṇini, the tradition, and Sanskrit's later life
lessons.point: Know how Pāṇini's grammar works, read its terms in commentaries, and place Sanskrit beside Pali, the Prakrits and modern languages

lessons.title: Review: part 7 as a whole
lessons.point: Translate a passage and build and correct sentences using everything taught so far

lessons.title: Reading 1: the Hitopadeśa, frame story and verses on learning
lessons.point: Read the opening of the Hitopadeśa (prelude verses 3–6 and the beginning of the frame story)

lessons.title: Reading 2: Nala and Damayantī, Mahābhārata 3.50.1–10
lessons.point: Read the opening of the Nala episode, the traditional first reading in Sanskrit

lessons.title: Reading 3: Nala and the swan, Mahābhārata 3.50.17–27
lessons.point: Read the swan's message, with its epic forms

lessons.title: Reading 4: Rāmāyaṇa 1.2.9–15, the first śloka
lessons.point: Read the story of how Vālmīki's grief became the first verse

lessons.title: Reading 5: Bhagavad Gītā 2.19–22, the self that is not slain
lessons.point: Read Kṛṣṇa's argument that the self neither kills nor is killed

lessons.title: Reading 6: Kālidāsa, Raghuvaṃśa 1.1–4
lessons.point: Read the opening of Kālidāsa's epic as a first taste of kāvya

lessons.title: Capstone: the Bhagavad Gītā, 1.1 and 2.47–48
lessons.point: Read the opening question of the Gītā and its most quoted teaching, on action without attachment to its fruits

lessons.title: Tables: nouns, adjectives and pronouns
lessons.point: Look up any nominal or pronominal ending

lessons.title: Tables: verbs and the principal parts of common roots
lessons.point: Look up any verb form, and the main forms of the commonest roots

lessons.title: Tables: sandhi
lessons.point: Look up any external or internal sandhi join

lessons.title: Glossary of terms and abbreviations, and annotated bibliography
lessons.point: Look up a grammatical term or abbreviation, and find where to read further
